studio: session scratchpad directory outside the repository; the agent was instructed to read/write nothing else and to use no other tool
isolation_note: isolation by instruction, not enforcement (freeze: isolation_is_by_instruction_not_enforcement=true). The subagent received the harness's standard global instruction files (user-level CLAUDE.md), which mention project names in passing; it received no repository path, no lane vocabulary, no mechanism description, and no world/result. The mechanical guarantee is the taxonomy-disjointness hostile (m2p2_taxa.py) run by m2p2_check.py over every authored byte.
emitter_review: line-by-line before first execution: imports = json only; the single open() is the required write of worlds.jsonl to the current directory; no os/sys/subprocess/socket/environ/thread usage
author_summary_verbatim: I authored 10 worlds in the studio directory (emit_worlds.py, worlds.jsonl generated by one run of the emitter, AUTHOR_NOTES.md), all ten with pairwise-distinct shapes: chunk counts 5-8, chunk-length profiles spanning all-2 (hc02), all-3 (hc04) and four mixes, minimum builder lengths using every value 4-8, and five different dyadic part-fraction triples (exact sums to 1.0). Design ideas covered: a purely linear 'binary ladder' and its sub1 mirror (hc01/hc09), a sqr-in-every-chunk even-length world (hc02), deliberately overlapping runs for multi-tiling ambiguity (hc03), a triads-only single-length pairing table (hc04), min length pinned at the ceiling (hc05), two never-canonical decoy chunks that leave no visible trace (hc06), a high-degree squaring tower (hc10), and two fixed-seed drawn controls (hc07/hc08, inline 64-bit LCG, seeds 7004 and 8002 recorded in intent and notes); the emitter's self-contained projector reports 31-1194 members per world, none empty, with all dead chunks confined to the decoy world as intended.
